blocks.heading_context: ## Layer 2: Why Convexity Is the Dividing Line
blocks.text: A set $C \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is **convex** if for all $x, y \in C$ and $\lambda \in [0,1]$, $\lambda x + (1-\lambda) y \in C$. A function $f$ is convex if its epigraph is a convex set, equivalently $f(\lambda x + (1-\lambda)y) \le \lambda f(x) + (1-\lambda) f(y)$.
